summary: When a fan picks a seat, one atomic update claims it for five minutes, so nobody else can grab it while they pay. The payment carries that claim's id, so a retry never charges twice, and an unpaid claim just expires.
explanation: ~1.7k joins/s (assume 10-minute rush), ~5k seat-map reads/s, ~1k hold writes/s on 50k rows — contention, not volume, is hard.
Two fans never hold the same seat

the hold is one conditional update setting status HELD and hold_expires_at = now + 5 min, only if the seat is available or its hold expired. One row-level winner; lapsed holds free themselves, so no sweeper race.
hold_id is the idempotency key on the charge and unique on the seat row, so retries replay the same result. A charge landing after the hold lapsed is refunded with the same key.

the Waiting Room admits signed-token batches sized to the hold write rate, and seat maps come from the Cache keyed by event_id. Fans over capacity wait; sold-out pages never touch the Inventory Database.
